question: An 11-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her parents because of a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed a low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache, followed by a facial rash 4 days later. The facial rash did not involve the perioral skin. Her temperature is 37.4°C (99.3°F). A photograph of the rash on her lower arms is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, headache" -> "Facial rash without perioral involvement" -> "Rash on trunk and extremities" -> "Mildly pruritic rash" -> "Recent history of fever and rash" -> "Viral exanthem likely" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Facial rash without perioral involvement" -> "Rash on trunk and extremities" -> "Mildly pruritic rash" -> "Recent history of fever and rash" -> "Viral exanthem likely" -> "Differentiate between common viral exanthems" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Facial rash without perioral involvement" -> "Rash on trunk and extremities" -> "Mildly pruritic rash" -> "Recent history of fever and rash" -> "Viral exanthem likely" -> "Consider Rubella, Erythema infectiosum, Exanthem subitum" -> 70%
analysis: The presentation of a low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, headache, and subsequent rash on the trunk and extremities, not involving the perioral skin, along with the given image of the rash on the lower arms, is most consistent with the diagnosis of Erythema infectiosum, also known as Fifth disease.
